what_it_does: Data centers consume a lot of electricity keeping their servers cool. Traditional cooling—blowing air over chips or pumping liquid through pipes—doesn't work well as chips get hotter and denser. This paper proposes using a manufacturing technique called Electrochemical Additive Manufacturing (ECAM) to build custom copper cooling structures that sit directly on hot chips and transfer heat straight into liquid with minimal resistance. The result is a more efficient cooling system that uses less power and space.
